summary: IDS feed 'breach' is degraded: 40.3% of TCP sessions (81/201) are one-way, violating IDS requirement for bidirectional traffic. All other visibility checks (duplicates, drops, overload, VLANs, encryption) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN is delivering only one direction per session to the IDS tool port. Likely SPAN configured as rx-only/tx-only or broker not aggregating both sides of the flow (asymmetric routing or separate TAPs) to the same tool port, so 81 of 201 sessions show only client->server or server->client.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP stream reassembly and stateful signature matching. With 40.3% one-way sessions the IDS cannot see handshakes, track state, or match bidirectional signatures, causing missed exploits and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregating both directions of each session to the same IDS port restores full flow visibility required for stateful IDS detection and eliminates one-way blindness.
